newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gen des Eaux confirms 96 profit forecast.
newsitem.headline: Gen des Eaux confirms 96 profit forecast.

text.p: Generale des Eaux expects to show a "modest" profit in 1996 after incurring a net attributable loss of 3.7 billion francs in 1995, chairman Jean-Marie Messier said in a newspaper interview, confirming earlier forecasts.
"I confirm that the group will return to a modest profit as of this year," Messier told French daily Le Figaro, adding profit will include exceptional items.
"For the next financial years and as of 1997, our results should better show the overall potential of our group," he said.
Messier also said that debt should "stabilise" in 1996, adding "a sharp (debt) reduction is our objective for 1997."
Messier said that Generale des Eaux had already sold 10 billion worth of assets since the beginning of 1996.
"For instance, we have almost completely withdrawn from Accor, we sold our stake in FNAC and we will review carefully any offer to acquire our stake in Blenheim," he said.
Messier ruled out selling part of the group's construction business but said Generale des Eaux was considering ways to rationalise it to help it weather strong competition.
"Rationalisation is necessary...we are in the final phase where decisions should be announced around mid-October," he said.
In the mobile communications sector, Messier said he appreciated the interest shown by Southwestern Bell and Vodafone in the Cegetel unit.
The two foreign companies are already shareholders of SFR, another unit of Generale des Eaux.
He also said that he was interested in forging links with a German partner in the long-distance communications sector.
But he stressed that these future partnerships would not change the group's shareholders structure.
